rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A concerns documentation placement (a new standalone design doc vs. folding into backend.md/frontend.md), while Finding B concerns a Prisma call pattern (empty-data `update` vs. `findUniqueOrThrow`) in document.service.ts. Fixing either leaves the other entirely intact.

panel.summary: New standalone top-level design doc for what is a single-PR backend fix, instead of folding into the canonical subsystem doc (backend.md / frontend.md)
panel.evidence: docs/design/README.md:122-128 states design docs are filed by validity and "Fold a single-PR note into the relevant doc as a concise subsection rather than keeping it as a standalone file"; CONTRIBUTING.md:55-59 says "Update the existing doc when evolving an area instead of creating parallel files." This change is a one-PR ordering fix touching the backend data model, REST list endpoints and Yorkie integration — all already described in docs/design/backend.md ("Database Schema", module list) and docs/design/frontend.md:416 ("Document list"). Creating docs/design/documents-last-modified.md plus a README row creates a parallel file for the documents-list area. (Counter-evidence: the Common section does host several single-feature top-level docs, e.g. context-menu.md, comments-mentions.md, so precedent is mixed.)

coderabbit.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts::consider using `finduniqueorthrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.summary: Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.evidence: **Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.** When `data` is empty, the current code calls `prisma.document.update({ data: {}, where })`. Prisma 6.6.0 may reject an empty `data` object at the client-validation level or generate invalid SQL (an `UPDATE` with no `SET` columns). The test mocks `prisma.document.update` so it wouldn't catch a real runtime failure. Returning the existing row via `findUniqueOrThrow` avoids the risk entirely and skips a needless write.
